# Custom tools tools

Define, test, inspect, approve and manage the project's own tools (Wander, composite and hosted).

9 tools in the `tools` category. Badges: **read-only** tools never change the project; **mutating** tools are undoable and attributed; **open-world** tools reach outside the engine and MCP clients ask before running them.

| Tool | Summary |
|---|---|
| [`tool_define`](#tool_define) | Create or update your OWN tool when no engine tool does what you need. |
| [`tool_test`](#tool_test) | Run a custom tool's tests, or one call with "args", as a DRY RUN: scene edits are rolled back and file writes skipped, so it is safe on tools that are not approved yet. |
| [`tool_list_custom`](#tool_list_custom) | Every custom tool of the project (and external tools hosted by connected clients) with its status — active, pending_approval, rejected, disabled, offline, invalid — kind, version, author and call counts, plus the project's policy. |
| [`tool_inspect`](#tool_inspect) | Full definition of a custom tool: code or steps, schemas, capabilities, limits, tests, status and why, approval (by whom, for which hash), stats (calls, failures, timing) and its recent calls and errors. |
| [`tool_remove`](#tool_remove) | Unregister a custom tool and delete its files (tools/&lt;name&gt;.tool.json and .wander) unless delete_files is false. |
| [`tool_approve`](#tool_approve) | A HUMAN approves (or rejects with approve:false) the current definition of a custom tool that needs approval (it mutates, writes files or reaches the network, or the policy is "ask"). |
| [`tool_enable`](#tool_enable) | Turn a custom tool off (it disappears from tools/list but keeps its files and approval) or back on. |
| [`tool_promote`](#tool_promote) | Copy a project's custom tool into your user library (~/.skywalker/tools) so other projects can install it with tool_define {"from_library": "user_x"} (their approval rules apply). |
| [`tool_policy`](#tool_policy) | Read or set who approves custom tools in this project (game.json customTools.policy): off (disabled), ask (every tool needs a human's approval), auto (default: read-only tools run at once, tools that mutate or write files need approval), trust (no approvals). |

### `tool_define` { #tool_define }

**Define a custom tool** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--mut" title="Changes the project; undoable and attributed">mutating</span>

Create or update your OWN tool when no engine tool does what you need. Kinds: "wander" — Wander code `fn run(args) ... end` that queries the scene and calls allowlisted tools (call_tool) under an instruction budget; "composite" — a pipeline of tool calls with templated args ({{args.x}}, {{steps.find.entities}}), for_each loops and a result mapping. Declare capabilities (read_scene, mutate, calls, files) as a minimal allowlist and add tests (args -> expect) — they run as dry runs before saving. Read-only tools become callable at once (as user_<name>, listed in tools/list); tools that mutate or write files wait for a human's approval (tool_approve) under the default policy. Updating merges your fields over the current definition. Example: {"name":"enemies_near","description":"Enemies within a radius of a point with their hp...","input_schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"radius":{"type":"number","default":10}}},"wander":"fn run(args)\n  let out = []\n  for e in find_all(\"enemy\")\n    if distance(e, (0,0,0)) <= args.radius then out.push({name: e.name, hp: e.hp}) end\n  end\n  return {enemies: out}\nend","tests":[{"args":{"radius":5},"expect":{"result":{"enemies":{"$type":"array"}}}}]}. docs/CUSTOM_TOOLS.md has recipes.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string |  | Tool name; it becomes user_&lt;name&gt; (lowercase, digits, underscores) |  |
| `title` | string |  | Short title (default: from the name) |  |
| `description` | string |  | For language models: what it does, when to use it, key arguments, an example |  |
| `category` | string |  | Permission category, e.g. scene, world, custom (default custom) |  |
| `kind` | string |  | Implementation (inferred: "wander" code or "steps") | `wander` `composite` |
| `input_schema` | object |  | JSON schema of the arguments ({type: object, properties, required}); property "default"s are filled in |  |
| `output_schema` | object |  | Optional JSON schema the result must match |  |
| `capabilities` | object |  | What the tool may do: an explicit allowlist (least privilege) |  |
| `capabilities.read_scene` | boolean |  | Query entities, components and vars (default true; false runs on an empty scene) |  |
| `capabilities.mutate` | boolean |  | Edit the scene, directly or through mutating tools (default false; needs a human's approval) |  |
| `capabilities.calls` | string[] |  | Tools it may call (call_tool / steps), e.g. ["scene_query", "entity_*"] |  |
| `capabilities.files` | object |  |  |  |
| `capabilities.network` | boolean |  | External tools only |  |
| `limits` | object |  | Hard limits |  |
| `limits.instructions` | integer |  | Wander instruction budget per call (default 1000000, max 50000000) |  |
| `limits.timeout_ms` | integer |  | Wall time per call (default 5000, max 120000) |  |
| `limits.max_output_bytes` | integer |  | Largest result (default 65536, max 1048576) |  |
| `limits.max_calls` | integer |  | Nested tool calls per call (default 100) |  |
| `wander` | string |  | kind wander: Wander code with `fn run(args) ... return {...} end` (saved to tools/&lt;name&gt;.wander). Builtins: call_tool, try_tool, tool_warn, tool_fail, read_file, write_file, list_files, file_exists, json_parse, json_text, tool_actor |  |
| `steps` | object[] |  | kind composite: tool calls in order (one undo step when the tool mutates) |  |
| `steps[].id` | string |  | Name for later templates ({{steps.&lt;id&gt;}}) |  |
| `steps[].tool` | string | yes | Tool to call |  |
| `steps[].args` | object |  | Arguments; {{args.x}}, {{steps.id.field}}, {{item}}, {{index}}, {{prev}}, {{x ?? default}} |  |
| `steps[].for_each` | any |  | Run once per element: a template giving an array, or a count |  |
| `steps[].as` | string |  | Loop variable name (default item) |  |
| `steps[].when` | any |  | Template; the step is skipped when it is false/empty |  |
| `steps[].continue_on_error` | boolean |  | Keep going when this step fails |  |
| `steps[].note` | string |  | Comment |  |
| `result` | any |  | kind composite: result mapping template (default: the last step's result) |  |
| `tests` | object[] |  | Checks run by tool_define and tool_test as dry runs |  |
| `tests[].name` | string |  | What it checks |  |
| `tests[].args` | object |  | Arguments for the call |  |
| `tests[].setup` | object[] |  | Tool calls run first (rolled back with the test) |  |
| `tests[].expect` | object |  | {ok, error: code, result: subset (with $gte $lte $gt $lt $len $contains $type), contains: text, max_ms} |  |
| `enabled` | boolean |  | Register it (default true) |  |
| `from_library` | string |  | Install a tool from the user library (tool_promote put it there) |  |
| `run_tests` | boolean |  | Run the tests before saving (default true); failing tests block the save |  |
| `validate_only` | boolean |  | Check and test without saving |  |

=== "Tool call"

    ```tool
    tool_define {"name": "enemies_near", "description": "Enemies within a radius of a point with their hp...", "input_schema": {"type": "object", "properties": {"radius": {"type": "number", "default": 10}}}, "wander": "fn run(args)\n  let out = []\n  for e in find_all(\"enemy\")\n    if distance(e, (0,0,0)) <= args.radius then out.push({name: e.name, hp: e.hp}) end\n  end\n  return {enemies: out}\nend", "tests": [{"args": {"radius": 5}, "expect": {"result": {"enemies": {"$type": "array"}}}}]}
    ```

=== "CLI"

    ```bash
    skywalker call tool_define '{"name": "enemies_near", "description": "Enemies within a radius of a point with their hp...", "input_schema": {"type": "object", "properties": {"radius": {"type": "number", "default": 10}}}, "wander": "fn run(args)\n  let out = []\n  for e in find_all(\"enemy\")\n    if distance(e, (0,0,0)) <= args.radius then out.push({name: e.name, hp: e.hp}) end\n  end\n  return {enemies: out}\nend", "tests": [{"args": {"radius": 5}, "expect": {"result": {"enemies": {"$type": "array"}}}}]}' --project my_game
    ```

=== "MCP request"

    ```json
    {
      "jsonrpc": "2.0",
      "id": 1,
      "method": "tools/call",
      "params": {
        "name": "tool_define",
        "arguments": {
          "name": "enemies_near",
          "description": "Enemies within a radius of a point with their hp...",
          "input_schema": {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {
              "radius": {
                "type": "number",
                "default": 10
              }
            }
          },
          "wander": "fn run(args)\n  let out = []\n  for e in find_all(\"enemy\")\n    if distance(e, (0,0,0)) <= args.radius then out.push({name: e.name, hp: e.hp}) end\n  end\n  return {enemies: out}\nend",
          "tests": [
            {
              "args": {
                "radius": 5
              },
              "expect": {
                "result": {
                  "enemies": {
                    "$type": "array"
                  }
                }
              }
            }
          ]
        }
      }
    }
    ```

### `tool_test` { #tool_test }

**Test a custom tool** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--ro" title="Never changes the scene">read-only</span>

Run a custom tool's tests, or one call with "args", as a DRY RUN: scene edits are rolled back and file writes skipped, so it is safe on tools that are not approved yet. Pass "definition" (same fields as tool_define) to try a draft without saving it. Returns per-test pass/fail with the compared values, logs and timing. Example: {"name":"user_enemies_near","args":{"radius":8}}

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string |  | Custom tool name |  |
| `definition` | object |  | An unsaved definition to try instead |  |
| `args` | object |  | Run one call with these arguments instead of the tests |  |
| `setup` | object[] |  | With args: tool calls run first (rolled back) |  |
| `setup[].tool` | string | yes | Tool |  |
| `setup[].args` | object |  |  |  |
| `filter` | string |  | Only tests whose name contains this |  |

=== "Tool call"

    ```tool
    tool_test {"name": "user_enemies_near", "args": {"radius": 8}}
    ```

=== "CLI"

    ```bash
    skywalker call tool_test '{"name": "user_enemies_near", "args": {"radius": 8}}' --project my_game
    ```

=== "MCP request"

    ```json
    {
      "jsonrpc": "2.0",
      "id": 1,
      "method": "tools/call",
      "params": {
        "name": "tool_test",
        "arguments": {
          "name": "user_enemies_near",
          "args": {
            "radius": 8
          }
        }
      }
    }
    ```

### `tool_list_custom` { #tool_list_custom }

**List custom tools** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--ro" title="Never changes the scene">read-only</span>

Every custom tool of the project (and external tools hosted by connected clients) with its status — active, pending_approval, rejected, disabled, offline, invalid — kind, version, author and call counts, plus the project's policy. include_library lists your user library (tool_promote); reload rescans tools/ for hand-edited definitions.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `include_library` | boolean |  | Also list the user library (~/.skywalker/tools) |  |
| `reload` | boolean |  | Rescan tools/*.tool.json first |  |

=== "Tool call"

    ```tool
    tool_list_custom {}
    ```

=== "CLI"

    ```bash
    skywalker call tool_list_custom '{}' --project my_game
    ```

=== "MCP request"

    ```json
    {
      "jsonrpc": "2.0",
      "id": 1,
      "method": "tools/call",
      "params": {
        "name": "tool_list_custom",
        "arguments": {}
      }
    }
    ```

### `tool_inspect` { #tool_inspect }

**Inspect a custom tool** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--ro" title="Never changes the scene">read-only</span>

Full definition of a custom tool: code or steps, schemas, capabilities, limits, tests, status and why, approval (by whom, for which hash), stats (calls, failures, timing) and its recent calls and errors. Use it to debug a tool or before changing it.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | Custom tool name |  |

=== "Tool call"

    ```tool
    tool_inspect {"name": "user_enemies_near"}
    ```

=== "CLI"

    ```bash
    skywalker call tool_inspect '{"name": "user_enemies_near"}' --project my_game
    ```

=== "MCP request"

    ```json
    {
      "jsonrpc": "2.0",
      "id": 1,
      "method": "tools/call",
      "params": {
        "name": "tool_inspect",
        "arguments": {
          "name": "user_enemies_near"
        }
      }
    }
    ```

### `tool_remove` { #tool_remove }

**Remove a custom tool** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--mut" title="Changes the project; undoable and attributed">mutating</span> <span class="sky-badge" title="May remove or overwrite data">destructive</span>

Unregister a custom tool and delete its files (tools/<name>.tool.json and .wander) unless delete_files is false. External tools are unregistered until their client registers them again.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | Custom tool name |  |
| `delete_files` | boolean |  | Delete its files (default true) |  |

=== "Tool call"

    ```tool
    tool_remove {"name": "Crate"}
    ```

=== "CLI"

    ```bash
    skywalker call tool_remove '{"name": "Crate"}' --project my_game
    ```

=== "MCP request"

    ```json
    {
      "jsonrpc": "2.0",
      "id": 1,
      "method": "tools/call",
      "params": {
        "name": "tool_remove",
        "arguments": {
          "name": "Crate"
        }
      }
    }
    ```

### `tool_approve` { #tool_approve }

**Approve a custom tool (human)** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--mut" title="Changes the project; undoable and attributed">mutating</span>

A HUMAN approves (or rejects with approve:false) the current definition of a custom tool that needs approval (it mutates, writes files or reaches the network, or the policy is "ask"). The approval is bound to the definition's hash: changing the tool needs approval again. Agents cannot approve; ask the human to use the editor's Studio > Tools panel or `skywalker call tool_approve '{"name":"user_x"}' --project DIR`.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | Custom tool name |  |
| `approve` | boolean |  | true approves (default), false rejects |  |
| `note` | string |  | Why (kept with the approval) |  |

=== "Tool call"

    ```tool
    tool_approve {"name": "user_props_along_spline"}
    ```

=== "CLI"

    ```bash
    skywalker call tool_approve '{"name": "user_props_along_spline"}' --project my_game
    ```

=== "MCP request"

    ```json
    {
      "jsonrpc": "2.0",
      "id": 1,
      "method": "tools/call",
      "params": {
        "name": "tool_approve",
        "arguments": {
          "name": "user_props_along_spline"
        }
      }
    }
    ```

### `tool_promote` { #tool_promote }

**Promote a tool to the user library** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--ro" title="Never changes the scene">read-only</span>

Copy a project's custom tool into your user library (~/.skywalker/tools) so other projects can install it with tool_define {"from_library": "user_x"} (their approval rules apply).

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | Custom tool name |  |

=== "Tool call"

    ```tool

    ```

    skywalker call tool_promote '{"name": "Crate"}' --project my_game

      "method": "tools/call",
      "params": {

### `tool_policy` { #tool_policy }

**Custom tool policy** <span class="sky-badge sky-badge--mut" title="Changes the project; undoable and attributed">mutating</span>

Read or set who approves custom tools in this project (game.json customTools.policy): off (disabled), ask (every tool needs a human's approval), auto (default: read-only tools run at once, tools that mutate or write files need approval), trust (no approvals). Agents may only make it stricter.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description | Values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `policy` | string |  | New policy (omit to read it) | `off` `ask` `auto` `trust` |

=== "Tool call"

    ```tool
    tool_policy {}
    ```

=== "CLI"

    ```bash
    skywalker call tool_policy '{}' --project my_game
    ```

=== "MCP request"

    ```json
    {
      "jsonrpc": "2.0",
      "id": 1,
      "method": "tools/call",
      "params": {
        "name": "tool_policy",
        "arguments": {}
      }
    }
    ```
